sources.note: p.39 entry 77 KWESTEN lists Dabe merely as one of the Kwesten villages (Ombe, Holmafin, Keder, Dabe, Takar, Betaf, Ansudu, Yamua); no Dabe wordlist; transcription conventions p.92: 'Stress and pitch are not indicated.'

sources.note: Glottolog: 0 descriptive references (only Lee & Wambaliau 2004 and ELCat as classification refs; bibliography = Oosterwal 1961, Smits & Voorhoeve 1994, Lee & Wambaliau 2004, Ethnologue). Wikipedia stub cites Ethnologue only. No ISO change requests. CrossRef: no relevant hits.
5 numerals from Wollaston (1912) under the name 'Takar' (identity doubtful); no stress marking.

sources.citation: Saad, George, Laura Arnold & Emma Peddie. 2025. Late Vernacular Production in Island Southeast Asia and the Pacific. Glossa Contact 1(1): 1-55. doi:10.82012/glossa.contact.2025.saad.et.al (ANU Open Research copy, 22 pp. PDF).
sources.note: no phonology content: a sociolinguistic paper on late vernacular production; for Dabe it reports only community-reported ages of passive (10) and active (20) competence summarised from Lee & Wambaliau 2004 (Table 2, p. 19 region) and lists Dabe among 32 LVP attestations (Appendix, item 13). Nothing on stress, accent or tone anywhere in the paper (the words stress/tone/phonology occur only incidentally).

sources.note: Map 1 legend lists 'Tor River Stock: 2. Dabe'; sec. 2.3.5.1 uses Dabe (DA) forms from Oosterwal 1961 in lexicostatistic cognate sets. No phonology of any Tor language.

sources.citation: Oosterwal, Gottfried. 1961. People of the Tor: A cultural-anthropological study on the tribes of the Tor territory (Northern Netherlands New-Guinea). Assen: Van Gorcum (PhD thesis, Utrecht). 322 pp.
sources.note: Contains the first Dabe wordlist (pp.274-277) and kin terms; might carry accent marks or a transcription note, though it is an ethnography.

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa. Peta Bahasa: Bahasa Dabe, Provinsi Papua (idb=351).
sources.note: Location (Kampung Dabe, Distrik Pantai Timur Barat), neighbours (Nengke east, Kejer west), dialectometry 94-100% different from neighbouring isolects; nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. New Guinea World: Orya-Tor River (family page with historical phonology); Tor Coast, Kwesten, Keijar subpages.
sources.note: Phonology section is '[under construction]' and empty. Lists sources (Oosterwal 1961:274-277, 76 terms; Smits & Voorhoeve 1994 'Kwesten of Dabe village' after Oosterwal; Lee & Wambaliau 2004:40-48 wordlist, 57-62 sentences) and gives pronouns after Lee & Wambaliau 2004:41 with one phonetic stress mark (2sg a'ke). No stress rule.
